elements.element: Licence scope is for Customer's business

offending_extra_words: Vendor retains Vendor Technology in accordance with Section 14.3.
and Vendor hereby irrevocably assigns to Customer all right, title, and interest in and to each Deliverable upon its creation
reasons: Preferred level incomplete: the redline flips ownership and adds an assignment, but supplies no perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to Vendor IP embedded in Deliverables. The margin comment's reliance on 13.2 is non-operative and cannot be credited, and Vendor Technology retention alone covers only named technology categories rather than any embedded Vendor IP.
Preferred level also lacks any express statement that Customer retains all rights in Customer Data; the definitional carve-out in 1.8 is not an affirmative retention.

Fallback is not satisfied and cannot be mixed in: no perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense Deliverables for Customer's business exists anywhere in the operative text (the prior Customer licence sentence was deleted).

Minimality fails: the operation rewrites the entire clause (changed-character ratio 0.736, above the 0.600 limit). Ownership could be flipped by changing "Vendor exclusively owns" to "Customer exclusively owns" plus a short assignment phrase, anchoring more unchanged text; the appended "Vendor retains Vendor Technology in accordance with Section 14.3" duplicates protection already given by Section 14.3 and the Deliverable/Vendor Technology definitions.
Intent is preserved: ownership now sits with Customer, no assignment of Customer Data or Customer IP to Vendor remains, and no undefined term or dangling licence mechanic is introduced.

To reach the locked preferred level, add a concise embedded-IP licence (perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to any Vendor IP embedded in Deliverables) and a short Customer Data retention sentence, without importing the fallback's worldwide/modify/sublicense wording.
